abstract: >
  This review explores the potential of bioinformatics and chemoinformatics
  tools to advance the exploration of natural extracts libraries (NELs).
  Although metabolomics has become a term used routinely in natural product (NP)
  research, the field remains focused on individual molecules or small sets of
  compounds, which restricts scalability. This narrow focus is mirrored in the
  computational handling of generated data, limiting broader insights. By
  challenging the traditional molecule-first paradigm—a framework historically
  shaped by practical constraints—we present our vision of using computational
  approaches to unlock the full potential of NELs, now and in the future.
